newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Closure on Palestinian areas not eased.
newsitem.headline: Closure on Palestinian areas not eased.

text.p: PLO officials said the Israeli army had yet to begin a promised easing of a closure on Sunday meant to enable more Palestinians to work in Israel.

"We were surprised to hear such reports of an easing of the closure because this did not happen," a PLO official at the labour ministry said. "We have made an application to the Israelis to give entry permits into Israel for 7,000 workers from the Gaza Strip. We have not received them yet."
Israeli military sources said it was unclear how long it would take before Israel completed security checks and issued work permits to the 15,000 labourers and 500 merchants.

An Israeli army spokeswoman said on Saturday that the closure would be further eased, raising the number of Palestinian workers in Israel from 35,000 to 50,000. The workers must be married and at least 30 years old, she said.
An additional 500 merchants would also be allowed entry, raising the total number of eligible merchants to 2,250.

Until 1994 Israel allowed some 60,000 Palestinians to work in the Jewish states. Since then it has imposed closures, easing them temporarily, only to reimpose them after suicide bombings by Moslem militants, most recently in February and March.
